title: Gaussian noise preserves the integral
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure. Define $(T_\rho f)(x)=\mathbb E[f(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,Y)]$, where $Y$ has that product standard Gaussian law. Then $\mathbb E[(T_\rho f)(X)]=\mathbb E[f(X)]$ for $X$ with the same law.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure
